penalties_applied.name: requires_physical_logistics
penalties_applied.reason: Sourcing, de-bloating, and shipping physical display hardware requires procurement, warehousing, and fulfilment — cannot be automated by Claude.

penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Hardware modification or curation (flashing displays, vetting suppliers, quality-checking units) requires physical hands-on work per order.

penalties_applied.name: b2c_at_scale_needed
penalties_applied.reason: Selling premium hardware to privacy-conscious consumers is a volume consumer play — unit economics only work at scale (hundreds of units), which a solo factory cannot reach.

rationale: The buyer is a vague consumer segment ('privacy-conscious households') with no demonstrated willingness to actually transact — one HN commenter theorizing a price point is not a paying customer. The product requires physical hardware sourcing, de-bloating/flashing displays, and fulfilment logistics that are entirely outside what a Claude factory can automate. Even setting aside the hardware problem, b2c consumer electronics is a capital-intensive, margin-thin, high-return-rate business that a solo non-technical operator cannot run sustainably.
solution_plan: A solo non-technical operator could NOT build this. The business requires a supply chain: sourcing displays from manufacturers or wholesalers, physically modifying or vetting them, warehousing inventory, and shipping to consumers. None of those steps are automatable by Claude. Even the 'software' adjacent version — a curated buying guide or affiliate referral site pointing to existing dumb displays — would earn trivial affiliate revenue and requires consumer SEO at scale. This is the wrong shape for this factory.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy_min (scored 2, floor 7), buildability_with_ai_min (scored 2, floor 6), buyer_clarity_min (scored 3, floor 6), and willingness_to_pay_min (scored 4, floor 5). Multiple hard gate failures plus physical logistics penalties.
